key_insight: Kidney-adapted AI predicted spatial gene expression from routine histology, linking tissue features to injury, repair and fibrosis programs.
clinical_relevance: This research could extend molecular characterization to archived kidney biopsies, but does not establish a clinical diagnostic or treatment-selection tool.
method: Adapted DeepSpot-M using paired histology and Visium data from 209 KPMP participants.
Evaluated predictions in held-out human biopsies and 567 rats with defined nephrotoxin exposures.
Generated 5.46 million virtual spots from 1,534 slides of 476 additional KPMP participants.
evidence_signal: Mean gene-expression correlation improved from 0.22 to 0.43 for each model’s 1,000 best-predicted genes; predictions preserved all 13 disease-marker directions and all 11 measured eGFR associations.
watch_item: Predicted expression is not a direct molecular measurement; generalizability and clinical utility require further validation, and this study concerns kidney disease rather than cancer drug discovery.
paper_title: Virtual spatial transcriptomics links kidney histopathology to disease-associated molecular programs
